reasons: Both answers are nearly identical in substance: correct literal-vs-identifier explanation, whitelist plus psycopg2.sql.Identifier with fixed ASC/DESC, escape_like, a case-insensitive Markup-based highlight that escapes before wrapping in <mark>, removal of |safe, the aborted-transaction warning and test lists. B adds a small public-name-to-column mapping and a slightly more concrete test expectation, while A has a marginally clearer loop-based highlight; neither difference is decisive. Both share the same minor inaccuracy about ORDER BY a string literal.

A: Claims ORDER BY 'created_at' silently sorts by a constant; PostgreSQL actually rejects a non-integer string constant in ORDER BY with an error.
B: Claims ORDER BY 'price' silently sorts by a constant; PostgreSQL actually rejects a non-integer string constant in ORDER BY with an error.
